title: Design a Rate Limiter
interviewPrompt: For today's Software Engineer interview, design a rate limiter.

beats.interviewer: For today's Software Engineer interview, design a rate limiter. Say 100 requests per user per minute.
beats.interviewee: Complete naive system: gateway checks an in-memory per-user counter, then either forwards to the service or returns 429. Full allow and deny path from beat one.
Same full path. Fixed-window burst: 100 at 0:59 and 100 at 1:00, all legal, 200 in two seconds.
beats.show: Same complete path. Fixed-window burst is the bug.

beats.interviewer: So go deeper. What do you use instead?
beats.interviewee: Rework the counter to a token bucket, and put it in Redis so every server shares state. Allow and deny exits stay wired.
beats.show: Rework: token bucket + Redis. Full allow/deny still complete.

beats.interviewee: Walk both exits on the full system: token left, pass to service. Bucket empty, 429 with Retry-After.
beats.show: Full path both ways: allow → Service, deny → 429.

beats.interviewee: Fixed-window is cheapest, sliding-log is exact, token bucket is the middle. Senior detail on this complete system: atomic Redis Lua so two servers cannot both admit.
beats.show: Same complete system. Atomic Lua check is the senior detail.
